reason: E2 directly supports that ultrafine-grained stainless steels show improved corrosion resistance due to greater Cr enrichment in the passive film, attributed to selective Fe dissolution and Cr oxidation. However, E1 only states that Cr is vulnerable to corrosion in molten salts, which does not support the proposed mechanism and may even conflict with the idea of a protective Cr-rich film in that environment. The hypothesis overstates support for the molten salt condition.
premises: Grain refinement increases grain boundary density in stainless steels
Enhanced grain boundary density promotes selective Fe dissolution and preferential Cr oxidation
This leads to faster formation of a Cr-rich passive film
The Cr-rich passive film improves corrosion resistance in aggressive environments
This mechanism applies to both aqueous and high-temperature molten salt environments
